data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** 52cd3ad71beeb9b9a40f02b6d0b07d67226d31d9
* **harness:** Claude Code Agent tool, isolation:worktree
* **context:** /dso:sprint waxen-sigma Layer-0 batch (4 parallel agents)

### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Upstream harness defect (infrastructure)

#### Expected Behavior
Every Agent dispatch with isolation:"worktree" runs in its own .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> worktree; the completion notification carries a <worktree> block; the sub-agent's git rev-parse --show-toplevel resolves to that isolated worktree.

#### Actual Behavior
3 of 4 Layer-0 agents isolated correctly (each notification carried a <worktree> block; agent worktrees present in git worktree list). The 4th agent (task b5fd-7682, dso:red-test-writer) ran WITHOUT isolation: its completion notification had NO <worktree> block, no agent-<id> worktree was ever created, and its git rev-parse --show-toplevel resolved to the SESSION worktree — so its files (tests/scripts/test-run-hermetic.sh + .test-index) landed staged in the session worktree.

The dispatch prompt did NOT contain any session-worktree absolute path (only SESSION_BRANCH branch name + SESSION_HEAD sha + relative paths), so this is NOT the prompt-path-leak failure mode (6b67-2aad / 1053-4ec3). It is a harness isolation-allocation flake: isolation was requested on the Agent call but not applied to that one dispatch.

#### Distinguishing signal
Presence/absence of the <worktree> block in the task-completion notification reliably separated isolated (5e96, 55c7, 315a) from un-isolated (b5fd) dispatches in the same batch.

### 3. Action History
Work was NOT lost: recovered by backing up the staged session changes to a patch, stashing, recreating a worktree-agent-b5fd-recovered branch from session HEAD, restoring the files + .test-index entry, then committing + harvesting like the others.

### 5. Skills and Workflows
* per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 1a 907d / Tier-2 RECOVERED_FROM_SESSION path is the documented recovery for exactly this; here it was handled manually.
data.title: [Claude Code harness]: isolation:worktree dispatch ran un-isolated -> sub-agent wrote to session worktree
